sample_unit: radiologist annotations on the CheXpert test set and label schemas from two public datasets and a vendor

links.outcome: Inter-radiologist agreement on CheXpert test set labels and reliability of majority-vote ground truth
links.effect: Agreement was high for pneumothorax and medical devices (>90%) but low for pneumonia and consolidation, where majority-vote ground truth was unreliable and depended on which radiologists annotated. Schema overlap across datasets and vendor was <50%.
links.quote: Among low agreement classes (pneumonia, consolidation), the labels assigned as "ground truth" were unreliable, suggesting that the result of majority voting is highly dependent on which group of radiologists is assigned to annotation.

unlisted_practices: Harmonizing labeling schemas and ontologies across imaging datasets and vendors
Adapting task design, annotation methods, and model training to account for label noise

screen.reason: Empirical analysis quantifying schema inconsistency and annotation label noise in medical imaging datasets (e.g., CheXpert) that hinder reliable AI deployment.
